page: Microsoft Azure E64-32s_v6 is a memory-optimized virtual machine instance based on Microsoft Hyper-V virtualization. Powered by an x86_64 Intel Xeon 8573C processor with clock speeds up to 4.2 GHz, the instance provides 32 dedicated vCPUs mapped across 16 physical cores with simultaneous multithreading enabled. The compute architecture features a 260 MB L3 cache, 2 MB L2 cache per core, and hardware acceleration via Intel Advanced Matrix Extensions (AMX) and AVX-512 vector instruction sets. Memory capacity is substantial at 512.0 GB, establishing a high allocation of 16.0 GB of RAM per vCPU.

The E64-32s_v6 features no bundled local disk storage and contains no discrete GPU accelerators. Because ephemeral or integrated NVMe storage is absent, all persistent I/O relies on remote attached network volumes, specifically supporting Azure Premium Storage. The absence of local disk requires planning for external storage throughput constraints when handling swap or intensive scratch disk tasks. Additionally, no complimentary public IPv4 addresses are provisioned with the instance.

Benchmark evaluations indicate exceptional memory subsystem throughput and robust compute metrics. The instance achieves strong large-block uncached memory read bandwidth of 246.92 GB/sec and write bandwidth of 141.39 GB/sec. Synthetic processing tests reflect strong results, with Geekbench recording 2143.0 for single-core and 17375.0 for multi-core performance. Single-threaded gzip compression performs in the upper quartile at 31.38 GB/sec. In addition, CPU-based machine learning inference achieves strong prompt processing speeds on medium models and high text generation on smaller models.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the constrained core profile of 32 vCPUs paired with a full 512 GB memory pool optimizes resource spending for software systems priced per CPU core. Workloads that exhaust memory long before exhausting compute cycles avoid unnecessary licensing expenses. The instance is recommended for enterprise relational database engines such as Microsoft SQL Server and Oracle, large-scale Redis in-memory caching tiers, and memory-intensive extract-transform-load (ETL) pipelines.

The instance bundles no local disk storage and zero discrete GPUs, relying entirely on remote Azure Premium Storage for disk operations. Benchmark evaluation demonstrates strong uncached memory bandwidth reaching 246.92 GB/sec read and 141.39 GB/sec write, alongside upper-quartile Geekbench scores and high compression throughput.
